title: termal_wait_delegations' default 300 s wait outlasts Codex's delegation tool timeout, and the serial bridge keeps polling after Codex gives up
outcome: Found by the Claude /review-code child in the w-33bee3bec3f0 review round 4 (delegation-0239f4f4-fe46-4b57-9961-974193f8d18e, session-8473). termal_wait_delegations waits 300 s by default (DEFAULT_DELEGATION_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS; at most 1,800 s). Codex ends a delegation tool call at the server's tool_timeout_sec, about 226 s once w-33bee3bec3f0 lands, 60 s by default before it. The bridge serves stdin one request at a time (run_delegation_mcp_bridge), so after Codex gives up it keeps polling until its own deadline. Codex's next tool call then waits in that queue, up to about 74 s at the default, and that time counts against the next call's own timeout. This predates w-33bee3bec3f0, which shrinks the gap. agent-delegation-sessions.md now describes the cut, but the tool description an agent sees does not.
acceptance: A Codex caller of termal_wait_delegations either gets a structured `timedOut: true` result before Codex's tool timeout (its wait is capped below the delegation server's tool_timeout_sec when the bridge serves Codex), or the tool description states the cap; and an abandoned wait no longer delays the next tool call past its own allowance; a test covers the default wait for a Codex-served bridge
